speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've been dealing with chronic left shoulder pain without any history of trauma. To help narrow this down, does the pain worsen when you lift your arm overhead or reach behind your back?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your age and the pain disrupting sleep, does the pain worsen significantly when you lie on your left side? Also, have you noticed any swelling or visible deformity around the shoulder joint?

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain worsening with extreme range of motion and sleep disruption, combined with your age and diabetes, raises concern for adhesive capsulitis or rotator cuff pathology. To better visualize the joint structures and rule out significant tendon tearing or calcific tendinitis, I need to see an image. REQUEST IMAGES: Left shoulder X-ray and MRI.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus Social history: No relevant social history provided

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of diabetes, age, and pain disrupting sleep significantly raises suspicion for adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder), though a rotator cuff tear is also possible given the mechanical symptoms. I have already requested your imaging. Please confirm if you have experienced any significant loss of both active and passive range of motion, such as inability to lift your arm even when someone else moves it for you.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have denied neck pain and neurological symptoms like numbness or weakness, we can rule out cervical radiculopathy.
